context.alert_text: Errors on the checkout tax function above 20 per minute

root_cause.hypothesis: Errors are caused by an unhandled application-level exception (TaxEngineError) inside the tax calculation engine code, triggered by certain input data (e.g. jurisdiction/line-item fields), rather than by a deploy, resource exhaustion, timeout, or throttling.
evidence: F3: code=TaxEngineError; level=ERROR appears in log lines
F5/F6: stack trace references tax/v2/engine.py at multiple line numbers
F7/F8: fields 'jurisdiction' and 'lines' appear near the error traceback
C3: no change/deploy in the 6h window rules out a bad deploy as the trigger
M1/M2/M6: timeout(10s) and memory(512MB) are far from the observed max duration (211.7ms) and memory used (~124MB), ruling out resource exhaustion
M4: throttles=0 rules out concurrency/throttling causes
ruled_out: Recent deploy/config change (C3 shows none in 6h)
Timeout (M1 vs M6 duration_max_ms=211.7 is far under 10s)
Memory exhaustion (M2=512MB vs F2 max_memory_used up to 124MB)

proposal.reasoning: The evidence points to a recurring application-level exception (TaxEngineError) in the tax engine code, not to infrastructure, deploy, timeout, memory, or throttling issues. No recent deploy exists to roll back, and no config change to revert. This requires a developer to inspect the TaxEngineError handling around jurisdiction/line-item parsing in engine.py; no automated remediation in the allowed set addresses a code defect safely.
proposal.expected_effect: A human investigates and patches the TaxEngineError root cause in the tax engine code, halting further error spikes.
